prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor store aisle with multi-tiered display shelves in the foreground (~0.5–1.2 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer and nearby person) and a wall with windows and a far room ~3–5 m behind them. In frames 1, 2, and 5, a person stands on the right at ~1.0–1.5 m from the camera wearer and ~0.5–1.0 m to the right of the shelves, with their lower body cropped out by the bottom frame edge and their torso occluding the background window. As the camera wearer turns left toward the shelves in frames 3–4 (moving the person out of view to the right) and turns back right in frame 5, the shelves remain within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m) while a chair appears in the background left of the aisle in frame 4 at ~3 m distance. Compared to the dimly backlit RGB frames, the depth map clearly separates the backlit person's silhouette and the tiered shelf geometry from the background, as well as the distant chair in frame 4. However, the depth map is unreliable on the glass windows (rendering them as flat, moderately near surfaces rather than transparent openings) and blurs fine boundaries between individual snack boxes on the shelves.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the person on the right in frames 1 and 2 (~1.0–1.5 m from the camera wearer, standing in front of the background windows with their lower body below the bottom frame edge) and a distant chair (~3 m away, behind and to the left of the shelf end-cap) in frame 4. Across the sequence, the person shifts slightly left and closer from frame 1 to frame 2 as the camera pans, disappears out of the right side of the view when the camera wearer turns left to face the shelves at arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m) in frames 3–4, and reappears on the right in frame 5 at ~1.5 m away. It makes the small black chair on the left of frame 4 immediately identifiable despite dark shadows in the RGB image. However, the map is highly unreliable across the scene: it completely misses all display shelves and almost all merchandise within arm's reach, misclassifies a carton on the lower-left shelf in frame 3 (~0.6 m away) as a 'book', and in frame 5 detects only a tiny fragment of the motion-blurred person's head while missing their entire torso.
descriptions.pose: The pose map places sparse yellow keypoints on the upper body and head of the person standing on the right in frames 1 and 2 (~1.0–1.5 m from the camera wearer, to the right of the shelves that lie ~0.5–1.0 m away). In frame 1, the vertical alignment of head and neck keypoints indicates the person is angled slightly leftward, whereas in frame 2 the horizontal shoulder bar and centered facial keypoints show the person facing and looking directly toward the camera wearer. Because the person's arms and lower body are cropped out below the bottom edge of the frame, no magenta hand skeletons appear, leaving it unconfirmed in the pose map whether their hands reach the nearby shelves (~0.5–1.0 m to their left). While the pose keypoints help clarify the person's head and shoulder orientation despite severe backlighting in the RGB frames 1 and 2, the map is unreliable overall: it provides only incomplete upper-body fragments in frames 1–2 and completely fails to detect the person in frame 5 due to motion blur.
